text: Lesson 21 built a real pipeline. Left unmonitored, a failed run means Overlook's appointment data for that day never lands in the database, and nobody knows until a report looks wrong days later — the same shape of problem Chapter 5 solved for the database itself.

Every pipeline run is recorded in Data Factory's Monitor hub — status, timing, and for a failed run, the specific activity and error that caused it. An alert rule on a Failed status, routed to the same on-call distribution Lesson 19 already uses, means a failed load gets noticed the same night it happens.

Before any alert fires, a retry policy on the Copy activity automatically re-attempts a transient failure, like a brief network blip. By the time the alert actually fires, a simple retry has already been ruled out — so the alert specifically means something real.

With the pipeline built and monitored, all five of Lesson 2's planned pieces are complete: infrastructure, security, HA/DR, automation, and ETL. Chapter 7 tests all of it together, starting with an unannounced disaster recovery drill.
